# EconPapers

> > EconPapers is a comprehensive economics research database powered by RePEc, providing access to working papers, journal articles, author profiles, and JEL classification codes.

EconPapers serves as a central access point to economics research literature, indexing content from RePEc (Research Papers in Economics). The platform offers searchable access to academic papers, author profiles through the RePEc Author Service, and institutional directories via EDIRC, making it an essential resource for economics researchers worldwide.

## Key Topics

- RePEc (Research Papers in Economics)
- EconPapers database
- JEL classification codes
- RePEc Author Service
- Working papers and MPRA
- Economics journal articles
- Author profiles and citations
- EDIRC institutional directory
- Economics research taxonomy
- Academic paper indexing
- Economics subject categorization
- Research literature database
- Economist directory

## Getting Started

- [EconPapers Homepage](https://econpapers.repec.org/): Main entry point to the EconPapers economics research database powered by RePEc

## Classification & Reference

- [JEL Classification Codes](https://econpapers.repec.org/scripts/jelsearch.pf): Complete reference for JEL codes used to categorize economics research by subject area

- [Dana Scott](https://econpapers.repec.org/RAS/psc871.htm): Research profile and publications for Dana Scott, Yale University Economics Department
- [Kenwin Maung](https://econpapers.repec.org/RAS/pma2990.htm): Research profile and publications for Kenwin Maung, University of Rochester
- [Ke Song](https://econpapers.repec.org/RAS/pso668.htm): Research profile and publications for Ke Song, Renmin University finance researcher

## Research Papers

- [Public-Private Partnership and Sustainable Development](https://econpapers.repec.org/article/nos00pard/175.htm): Research article examining PPP as a tool for sustainable territorial development
